A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIRE research and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, component ablations, perturbation tests, and visual analyses in Section 4, with additional visualizations in supplementary Section 6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and supplementary visualizations in Section 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain identical frequency-mask refinement, autoencoder reconstruction, error-map concatenation, classifier, and training objectives. Renaming Section 3.1 does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DiffusionForensics subsets, self-collected dataset with five newer generators, and perturbation scenarios. Supplementary examples cover the same real and generated images.

E2.justification: CNNDet, AEROBLADE, DIRE, and FakeInversion retain the same participation in the benchmark comparisons and robustness evaluation. No comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, sample counts, preprocessing, AUC and ACC metrics, training settings, and perturbation procedures are unchanged. Both retain batch size 16 and 100 training epochs.

E4.justification: The preset-mask and loss-term ablations in Tables 3–4, robustness tests in Figure 7, and visual analyses in Figures 5–6 and supplementary Figures 8–13 are identical.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4, plotted robustness results in Figure 7, and qualitative findings in the main and supplementary visualizations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 and their mathematical explanations are unchanged, including the diffusion processes, frequency masks, reconstruction errors, and losses. Neither version adds formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about frequency-guided reconstruction, end-to-end detection, generalization, and robustness.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretation of mid-frequency reconstruction information and the same severe-blur limitation relative to FakeInversion in Section 4.4. No applicability boundary or mechanism explanation changes.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, loss weights, optimizer settings, SD-v1.5 autoencoder choice, NVIDIA A100 hardware disclosure, and data-processing details are identical. Access information and hyperlink targets also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 50 references are unchanged, including the positioning of FIRE relative to earlier reconstruction-based detectors.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the affiliation typo 'CyberSpcae' to 'CyberSpace', renames Section 3.1 from 'Diffusion Reconstruction Error' to 'Diffusion Reconstruction Pipeline', and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Other wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 13 figures and four tables retain identical graphics, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layout and supplementary visualizations are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The affiliation correction and revised Section 3.1 heading provide slight editorial polish. The scientific explanations, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and supplementary material remain identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
